note: Passage 3704 (Pro 1:7-8) — the motto. fear-of-the-LORD = the human's reverent awe (God as target, locus internal). despise (buz) = the fool's contempt, target=wisdom (two-axes). Descent (fools despise) read at full weight. 'Hear' upgraded to characteristic.

dims.v: the fear of the LORD — reverent awe before God
revering God as the very beginning/first-principle of knowledge
the LORD (God as the object of the fear)
welded to knowledge as its beginning (reshit) — fear is the door to knowing

the programmatic claim: knowledge does not begin in intellect but in a DISPOSITION of the inner life toward God (reverence). God is the target/arena; the fear itself is the human interior state. This anchors the whole book.
knowledge — the knowing that fear of God opens
knowledge as the fruit whose beginning is the fear of God
welded to the fear of the LORD as its root
daat is here the crown, not the entry — its beginning lies outside itself in reverence; knowledge is thus made dependent on a moral-religious disposition.
fools — the morally-obstinate who reject wisdom
the fool as the one who despises wisdom and instruction
welded to despising (buz); the fool is defined by his contempt
evil (the moral fool) is set as the antithesis of the God-fearer in the SAME verse: reverence begins knowledge, contempt refuses it. The fool is a disposition, not mere ignorance.
to despise — to hold wisdom in contempt
holding wisdom and instruction in contempt, refusing them
the defining act of the fool (264850)
buz is the DESCENT-operation — contempt turned on the very goods the book offers. Read at full weight: the fool's inner posture is active despising, not passive lack.
wisdom — here the object the fool despises
wisdom as the good held in contempt by the fool
paired with instruction (musar) as the despised goods
chokmah is the target of buz here (two-axes: its own char AND despise's object). The same good that reverence gains, contempt refuses.
the one who should receive it
paired with wisdom as the twin good despised
musar (discipline) recurs, now as an object of contempt — the fool refuses not just knowledge but the corrective shaping. Distinct occurrence from its 1:2-3 uses.
hear — the son commanded to receptive listening
heeding the father's instruction (an imperative of the will's attention)
set against the fool's despising — the son hears where the fool refuses
the imperative shama is the countermove to the fool's buz in the same passage: obedient listening vs contempt. Read as characteristic (the receptive-attentive operation).
the father's instruction — parental discipline to be heeded
the father's shaping discipline, the object of the son's hearing
paired with the mother's teaching (torah) in the parallel line
musar here is CONCRETE and relational — a father's discipline (not abstract), the thing the son's shama takes in; the target-endpoint of 264854.
